reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the general principle that microstructural features (dislocations, precipitates) pin domain walls and increase hysteresis, but neither passage addresses FeMnNiGeSi HEAs, thin-film/nanoribbon geometries, or the specific annealing intervention proposed. The key premises about as-deposited inhomogeneity causing pinning and the efficacy of the 350 °C/30 s anneal are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Local atomic inhomogeneity and residual stresses in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi HEA thin films create defect sites that pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain wall pinning broadens the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles.
Rapid thermal or pulsed laser annealing at ~350 °C for ~30 s can relieve local stresses and enhance chemical homogeneity without significant grain growth.
Reducing pinning centers enables more reversible domain wall motion, sharpening the magnetocaloric entropy change and improving cycle frequency.
Microstructural barriers that impede dislocation motion also pin magnetic domain walls, increasing hysteresis.
